review.verdict: The frame drops nearly all the load-bearing props from the brief — no brake lever, the scissors read as a stray crosshair, and the FAKE note is glued to the cloud instead of held by the officer — leaving two generic, near-identical flanking figures and a joke that doesn't land; it also recycles a recent blue/yellow composition. Fails.
revisionNotes: Add the missing 'lever' component (BRAKE label) attached to the exec on the left-third — the emergency-brake half of the joke isn't in the frame at all.
Rebuild 'cord-cut' as a recognizable giant pair of scissors with a yellow glow at the cut point; right now it renders as a tiny crosshair icon that reads as a glitch, not a prop.

Reattach the 'note' (FAKE label) to the officer's raised hand at right-third instead of pasting it onto the side of the cloud — as placed it looks like a loose tag on the cloud, not something a person is holding up.
Differentiate exec and officer: give them distinct poses/holds (one gripping down on the lever, one raising the note) instead of two mirror-identical yellow-shirted figures with 'holds: none'.
Spread the three vignettes to left-third / center-third / right-third per the brief instead of clustering everything in the vertical center; there's a lot of dead space top and bottom of the square.
Palette/composition (blue grid bg + two yellow-shirted humans flanking a center figure) closely echoes a recent slopper panel; shift a pose or accent color to read as fresh.

warnings: "lever-label" (label) was moved 23 px, 0 px to stay inside the safe area
"officer" extends outside the safe area in the final frame (x 676…1048, y 352…842)

review.verdict: Cast and concept are on-brief, but the three key actions are undersold: the exec isn't gripping the lever, the officer points off-frame instead of holding up the note (which floats disconnected near the cloud), and the officer clips the safe area — plus the layout repeats a recent blueprint-row template. Fails the average threshold.
revisionNotes: Reconnect the "lever" to the exec's hand instead of floating beside his hip: attach it at his grip point, scale to ~1.5, and set his pose to "pull" with a backward lean so the BRAKE action reads without relying on the label.

The "note" (FAKE) currently floats up near the cloud, disconnected from the officer's hand — re-anchor it directly above the officer's raised hand and change his pose from "point" to a hold-up gesture so he's visibly displaying the tag.
Officer breaches the safe area on the right (lint: x 676-1048); pull him inward ~40-60px or drop scale to 1.0 so his arm clears the margin.

Scale the cord-scissors prop up to ~1.4 and brighten/enlarge the yellow spark at the cut point — at current size the "giant scissors" cutting the cord reads as a faint squiggle, not the key visual beat of the piece.

This three-figure, blueprint-grid, yellow-accent composition (person/robot/person in a row) closely repeats recent sloppers; stagger the vignettes or vary the palette accent so it doesn't read as a template reuse.
Give the exec a clear grip/lean pose so pulling the brake is obvious at a glance, rather than standing neutrally next to a small unrelated lever shape.

warnings: "exec" (human) was moved 11 px, 0 px to stay inside the artboard

review.verdict: Fails: the three parallel vignettes collapse into one cluttered center cluster where the BRAKE label is buried in the robot's head/spark glow and the giant scissors are nearly invisible, so the brake-lever/cut-cord/fake-note joke doesn't read in 3 seconds despite correct, kind casting.
revisionNotes: The exec's -50px offset pushes it into the robot's space, and the lever (attached to exec's right side, scale 1.5) lands directly behind the robot's head — move exec back toward true left-third with no negative x-offset so the lever clears the robot.
The BRAKE label is only legible as 'RAKE' because it overlaps the yellow spark glow and the robot's antenna — separate the lever vignette from the cord-scissors vignette with real horizontal space.

The giant scissors are nearly invisible, buried behind the robot's head with only thin crossed lines showing — scale the cord-scissors prop up and offset it clear of the robot so the blades and handles read as scissors.

The FAKE note floats near the cloud rather than visibly in the officer's hand — switch officer's pose to a single raised arm pointing at the note so the attachment reads as 'holding it up', not a stray caption.

Re-stagger the three vignettes into distinct left/center/right thirds with visible gaps; right now exec, lever, bot, and scissors all overlap in one central cluster instead of reading as three parallel moments.

This blueprint navy/yellow palette with a robot flanked by two plain humans is close to several recent pieces (the 'TOO LATE' and 'Missing Billions' tiles) — vary the palette accent or figure arrangement to stand apart.
